title: Accessibility
shortDescription: Accessibility is a powerful tool that allows you to determine whether networks provide sufficient access to members in a geographic area using standards detailed within a specification.
body:
Accessibility is a powerful tool that allows you to determine whether networks provide sufficient access to members in a geographic area using standards detailed within a specification. Accessibility is a premium feature of Network360 and may not be available to all users. ### Navigation To navigate to this module, click on one of the following modules on the left side bar navigation menu: **Competitive Analysis**, **Sales Tools**, **Compliance**, or **Broker Tools**. Then select **Accessibility**. This brings you to the **Manage Accessibility Analyses** page.

Manage Accessibility Analyses Page
On the Manage Accessibility Analyses page, you can view a grid which shows all the analyses and their status within your selected project. * By clicking the **Action Filter** icon in the top right corner of the grid, you can choose which columns display within the grid: * **Name** * **Description** * **Status** * **Population File** * **Specialty Mapping** * **Network – This is your Base Network** * **Specification** * **Last Updated** * **Created By** ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/1-actionfiltercolumns.png) * To change the sort order of a column, click on the column header. * Filter options are below the column headers: * Type into a blank field to search for your desired result, or * Select from the dropdown list **Status Definitions** * **Queued** – displays when many analyses are run at the same time and the analysis is pending. * **In Progress** – displays while the analysis is in progress. * **Suspended** – displays after the project has been re-imported/promoted. This indicates that the analysis needs to be run again to see the results. * **Incomplete** – displays for multiple reasons: * Some of the analysis criteria has been deleted (e.g. a population file, specialty mapping, specification, or network). * A published Model Network changes to Draft status. **Note**: Hovering over this status will display a tool tip pop-up identifying the specific issue. * **Ready** – displays when the analysis is ready to be viewed. Note: Editing an analysis in Ready status might require the analysis to be prepared or performed again. * **Failed** – displays for multiple reasons. Hovering over this status will display a tool tip pop-up identifying why the analysis failed. After a Project is refreshed, the Status will change to **Suspended** or **Incomplete** based on availability of the analysis components. If you view an analysis that uses a different specialty mapping than your currently selected Specialty Mapping, the specialty mapping will update to match the mapping that is used within the analysis. **Note**: Only Administrator users will be able to edit or delete other users’ Accessibility analyses.

Creating a New Accessibility Analysis
To execute a new Accessibility analysis, you will need the following pieces of information: * **Population File** * **Network Selection** * **Specification** ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/2-createnewanalysis.png) * **Name** – Give your analysis a name. This is a required field. * **Description** – Add a description of your analysis. This is optional. * **Population File** – This is a required field. For more information on using and creating a Population file, click here * **Base Network** - Select a network that will be used as a benchmark. This is a required field. * **Comparison Network** – This is an optional field. * Select one or more comparison networks, or * Leave the field blank – By not making a selection, an analysis will be performed on the Base Network only. * **Report Grouping** - Report Grouping determines how your results will be grouped on the **Geographic Summary** tab. For example, if you select **County** then you will see a section for each County associated with your population file. This is a required field. **Notes:** * Only the **Base Network** is considered in the **Access Map** and **Gap Map** results. * **Accessibility** will be calculated for the **Comparison Networks** as well, but they will not be evaluated in these maps. * If more than six networks are selected in total, the **Hospital Report** will not be available in the PDF export, though it will still be viewable in the application. * **Specification** – This is a required field. For more information on using and creating a **Specification**, click here
